newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: RACISM FORUM ORGANISER SAYS HOWARD HAS FAILED
An organiser of a racism forum to be held in Newcastle next week says the Prime Minister has forgotten to remind people that inciting racial hatred or violence is illegal.
Paul Collins says John Howard has failed to show leadership in the ongoing racial debate.
Mr Collins says Mr Howard needs to emphasise to the community that free speech needs to be responsible.
Mr Collins says there's a danger that without responsibility, you get misinformed people making outlandish statements which have no positive effect.
The forum will feature speakers from migrant and Aboriginal support groups, local government, and the the Anti Discrimination Board.
MARITIME UNION ANGERED BY DEMOCRAT'S DEAL

The Democrats admit unions affecting trade related industries will face heavy fines under the Federal Government's industrial relations bill...but say the Maritime Union is asking for rights it never had.
The Maritime Union says it's disappointed with the Democrats because they were under the impression they would negotiate to have secondary boycott bans removed from the bill completely.
Instead, the provisions will now be contained in the trade practices act.
The union says if it took action such as boycotting the loading of woodchips onto ships, it would be liable to fines of up to A$750,000.
WATERHOUSE TO PAYOUT FORMER STABLEHANDS
Sydney trainer Gai Waterhouse and her father TJ Smith have been ordered to pay A$17,000 in backpay to a former employee and the estate of another.

The Chief Industrial Magistrate's court in Sydney had heard the two men were employed as stablehands at Ms Waterhouse's Tulloch Lodge and had not been paid overtime as set out in the racing industry award.
Ms Waterhouse had told the court there was no paid overtime, save for three hours on Sunday, the trade-off being a share of the horses' winnings.
On evidence from the Department of Industrial Relations, the court found the men had been underpaid and directed they be paid a total of A$17,000.
ANTI-EUTHANASIA BILL EXPECTED TO GO TO A COMMITTEE
The Senate is expected to refer Kevin Andrews' Private Members Bill on euthanasia to a committee which would report in early February next year.
The Senate Selection of Bills Committee, which has representatives from all parties, looks at legislation which is due to come from the House of Representatives to the Senate.
The Committee recommends the bill should be considered by the Senate Legal and Constitutional Affairs Committee before its debated in the Senate.
The Senate is expected to decide this afternoon whether to refer the bill to a committee.
EXTRADITION OVER INTERNET PORNAGRAPHY CLUB
American FBI Agents have begun an extradition process for a Canberra man accused of belonging to an international "Internet Child Pornography Club."
It's alleged the man and 15 other Internet users, formed a password-restricted Internet chat room, called the "Orchid Club", which produced and traded "home made" child pornography.
A joint investigation between the Australian Federal Police and American FBI Agents led to the man's arrest earlier this year.
Australian Federal Police Spokesman Eric Myer says if convicted the man could spend up to 30 years in an American jail.
